## 401 N Wabash Ave — Zoning & Development Evaluation

---

### 1. Zoning District Currently in Effect

This parcel (PIN 17101350381067) is zoned **PD 835** — Planned Development No. 835, adopted under City ordinance **No. 13559**. This is the authoritative classification per the City of Chicago's official GIS zoning layer. You can verify it on the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Ordinary Base Zone or Something Else?

This parcel is **not** governed by an ordinary base zoning district. It is governed by a **Planned Development (PD)**, which is a site-specific, negotiated zoning instrument approved by the City Council under its own bespoke ordinance. The PD supersedes and replaces the standard bulk, density, use, and parking standards that would otherwise apply under the base district — meaning you cannot simply look up a B2 or DX table; the governing document is **PD 835's ordinance text itself (Ord. 13559)**. Under [1], buildings in "D" districts (which typically underlie downtown PDs) have no maximum height limits by right and require Planned Development review above certain thresholds — but again, for this parcel the PD ordinance controls directly.

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards

> ⚠️ **Critical caveat:** The specific bulk, density, FAR, height, setback, and unit-density standards that apply to this parcel are **contained in PD 835's ordinance text (Ord. 13559)**, which was not retrieved in full. The Municipal Code sections in context govern other district types (R, M, B/C, and general D districts) and **do not directly set the standards for this PD**. What can be said with confidence from the retrieved code:

- **Maximum building height:** There is no statutory maximum height limit in Downtown "D" districts [1]; however, PD review is required above the thresholds in [1], and the PD ordinance itself may set a project-specific height cap. Per [5], Planned Development standards require buildings on Wabash Avenue between the Chicago River and Ida B. Wells Drive to avoid upper-story setbacks below 55 feet of height.
- **Setbacks:** In DC, DX, and DS districts, no side setbacks are required; rear setbacks of 30 feet apply only to floors with dwelling units, with exemptions for DC-12, DX-12, DC-16, and DX-16 [1]. **However, PD 835 may override these.**
- **FAR, lot area, and unit density:** These are **not determinable** from the retrieved data. They are specific to PD 835's ordinance text.

**To obtain the authoritative bulk standards**, you must pull the actual text of **PD 835 / Ord. 13559** from the City Clerk's legislative database at [chicago.legistar.com](https://chicago.legistar.com) or the Department of Planning & Development (DPD).

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

The following apply to this parcel:

- **Planned Development (PD 835 / Ord. 13559):** The governing zoning instrument. All development must comply with the PD ordinance. Any material change requires a PD amendment approved by the Chicago Plan Commission and City Council.
- **Transit-Oriented Development — CTA Rail:** The parcel is within the CTA TOD overlay (within 0.2 miles of the Grand Red Line station). However, see Item 5 below — because this is a PD, the PD ordinance governs parking and density rather than the standard TOD code.
- **Transit-Oriented Development — Metra:** Also within the Metra TOD overlay (Millennium Station, 0.37 miles). Same governance note applies.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** This parcel is in an ARO zone, meaning residential development or entitlements triggering ARO will require affordable unit set-asides or in-lieu fees under [2] and §2-44-085. The Near North Side community area has 20 ARO housing projects totaling 1,010 affordable units currently recorded.
- **No landmark or historic district:** The parcel is not in a Chicago Landmark District, is not a designated landmark building, is not in a National Register historic district, and is not subject to lakefront protection.
- **No Special Service Area (SSA)**, no Planned Manufacturing District (PMD), no ADU area, and no special district designation apply.
- **Flood Zone X (Minimal Hazard):** FEMA designates this parcel as Zone X — Area of Minimal Flood Hazard. It is **not** a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not typically required.
- **Brownfield sites nearby:** Several EPA-listed brownfield properties are registered in the broader community area (including the Bloomingdale Park Trail site and Gateway Park Industrial Complex). While none appear immediately adjacent, environmental due diligence is advisable for any ground-disturbing work.

---

### 5. Parking Requirements and Transit-Related Reduction

Because this parcel is governed by **PD 835**, the PD ordinance itself controls parking minimums — standard base-district parking tables and the TOD parking reduction formula under §17-10-0102-B do **not** automatically apply here. As the transit-overlay data confirms: *"Planned Development: the PD ordinance governs parking and density."* The specific parking requirement must be read from Ord. 13559 directly. You should also confirm with DPD whether any PD amendment has modified the original parking schedule.

---

### 6. Maximum FAR and Building Height

- **By the Municipal Code alone:** Downtown "D" districts have **no statutory maximum building height** [1]. There is no universal FAR cap stated in the retrieved code for D districts.
- **In practice for this PD:** PD 835 (Ord. 13559) will contain a **project-specific FAR and height envelope** negotiated at approval. The building currently on-site is 92 stories (per county footprint data) with approximately 2,612,396 sq ft of floor area on a ~98,349 sq ft land parcel — implying a realized FAR of roughly **26.6:1**, consistent with a major high-rise Planned Development. Any new or modified development would be constrained by whatever the PD ordinance specifies, and any increase would require a **PD amendment**.

---

### Confidence Assessment

| Item | Confidence | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Zoning classification (PD 835) | **High** | City GIS authoritative layer, Ord. 13559 |
| PD governs (not base district) | **High** | Confirmed by regulatory overlay data |
| No height limit in D districts | **High** | Municipal Code [1] |
| Specific FAR/height/setback for PD 835 | **Cannot determine** — PD ordinance text not retrieved | Must obtain Ord. 13559 |
| ARO zone applicability | **High** | City regulatory overlay confirmed |
| TOD overlay applicability | **High** | City regulatory overlay confirmed |
| Parking standard for this PD | **Cannot determine** — PD ordinance controls | Must obtain Ord. 13559 |
| Flood zone | **High** | FEMA Zone X confirmed |

---

### How to Verify

1. **PD 835 ordinance text (Ord. 13559):** Search [Chicago Legistar](https://chicago.legistar.com) for ordinance 13559, or contact DPD's Zoning Division at (312) 744-5777.
2. **Zoning map:** [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning)
3. **ARO requirements:** Chicago Dept. of Housing, (312) 744-0060, or §2-44-085 of the Municipal Code.
4. **Cook County property records:** Use PIN 17101350381067 at [cookcountyassessor.com](https://www.cookcountyassessor.com).
